scenes.visual: photo of a young Indian man in a hoodie sitting on the parapet of a flat city rooftop at night, seen from behind and slightly to the side, looking up at a clear dark sky full of stars, one bright steady golden dot above the horizon, warm city lights glowing far below, the man and rooftop in the lower half of the frame, no readable text, no logos

narration.en: Why do *stars* twinkle at night, but *planets* don't?

scenes.visual: 2D animation: a star's light zig-zags through moving warm and cold air pockets down to an eye

narration.en: Starlight flies straight through space. Then it hits our *air*, full of moving warm and cold pockets, and each one *bends* it.
narration.hi: Taare ki roshni space mein seedhi aati hai. Phir hamari *hawa* mein garam aur thande pockets milte hain, aur har pocket use *mod* deta hai.

scenes.visual: photo of a deep dark night sky over a quiet Indian village, silhouetted coconut palm trees and a small house roof along the bottom, one very bright white star in the middle of the frame with a soft glow, many faint stars around it, no moon, no readable text

narration.en: A star is so far away, it's just one tiny *point* of light. So every bend makes it jump: *scintillation*.
narration.hi: Taara itna door hai ki wo bas ek chhota sa *point* dikhta hai. Toh har mod pe wo hilta hai. Ise kehte hain *scintillation*.

scenes.visual: 2D animation: left a star as one point with one zig-zag ray (flickers), right a planet disc with many rays (steady)

narration.en: Planets are closer, so they're tiny *discs*. Their light comes from many points, and the wobbles *cancel out*.
narration.hi: Planets paas hain, isliye chhoti *disc* jaise dikhte hain. Roshni kai points se aati hai, toh jhatke *cancel* ho jaate hain.

scenes.visual: photo of a calm beach in India just after sunset, deep blue sky with a thin orange glow at the horizon, one bright white star low in the sky just above the sea, a wooden fishing boat resting on the wet sand in the foreground, wide shot from the sand, no people, no readable text

narration.en: Stars low near the *horizon* twinkle the most, because their light crosses much *more air*.
narration.hi: *Horizon* ke paas wale taare sabse zyada timtimate hain, kyunki unki roshni bahut *zyada hawa* paar karti hai.

scenes.visual: 2D animation: above the air a satellite sees a steady star, below the air a person sees it twinkle

narration.en: And above the air, out in *space*, stars don't twinkle at all. They shine *steady*.
narration.hi: Aur hawa ke upar, *space* mein, taare bilkul nahi timtimate. Wahan wo *steady* chamakte hain.

scenes.visual: photo of two young Indian friends, a man and a woman in light jackets, standing on a city rooftop at night seen from behind, the woman pointing up at a bright steady golden dot in the dark starry sky, soft warm light from a doorway, the two friends in the lower half of the frame, no readable text

narration.en: Tonight, find a bright dot that *doesn't* twinkle. It's often a *planet*. Send this to your stargazing friend.
narration.hi: Aaj raat aisa chamakta dot dhoondo jo *timtimata nahi*. Wo aksar *planet* hota hai. Ye apne stargazing dost ko bhejo.

en.title: Why do stars twinkle, but planets don't? #shorts
en.description:
Why do stars twinkle? Starlight is bent back and forth by moving warm and cold pockets in our air (scintillation). A star is just one point of light, so it flickers; planets are tiny discs, so the wobbles cancel out. Star or planet? The steady one is often a planet. AI animation.

Sources: Britannica, WorldAtlas, Star Walk

en.caption:
Why do stars twinkle, but planets don't? ✨
Moving warm and cold air bends starlight back and forth, and a star is just one point, so it flickers. That's also why planets don't twinkle: they're tiny discs, so the wobbles cancel out. Star or planet? The steady dot is often a planet.
Did you ever notice this? 👇
